name: CPU Perf: Disable Forced 1s Bun.gc Interval
description: Neutralizes the unconditional once-per-second forced full garbage collection (setInterval(Bun.gc,1000).unref()) in the headless/startup path. Mirrors the 'Forced GC Every Second' finding from denysvitali/claude-code-patches, which observed 7 HeapHelper threads doing continuous marking work. Implemented as a same-length binary edit changing the 1000ms delay literal to 1e15 (~31,700 years), effectively disabling the manual GC while keeping Bun's adaptive GC intact. The upstream project's other CPU patches are runtime NODE_OPTIONS monkeypatches (reference-equality interception of setInterval, heap capping, telemetry/caching) that do not correspond to a single unique same-length binary string and are not reproduced here.

provenance.author: denysvitali
provenance.derived_by: anchored against pristine 2.1.158 using 2.1.88 source ref

operations.rationale: Upstream FINDINGS_2.1.45.md Finding 1: forced setInterval(Bun.gc,1000) causes continuous full-GC marking work. Changing the 1000ms delay to 1e15 (same length, 4 chars) makes the timer effectively never fire, disabling the manual GC without changing byte count or breaking JS validity. .unref() is preserved.
